name: Articles: A, An, and The
description: Practice choosing articles for first mentions, known things, and common sound patterns.

cards.front: Complete this first mention when any notebook will do: “I need ___ notebook for class.”
cards.answer: I need a notebook for class.
cards.explanation: Use “a” before a singular countable noun that is not specific and begins with a consonant sound.
cards.example: She brought a pencil to the workshop.
options: I need a notebook for class.
I need an notebook for class.
I need the notebook for class.

cards.front: Complete this first mention of one umbrella: “She packed ___ umbrella because rain was expected.”
cards.answer: She packed an umbrella because rain was expected.
cards.explanation: Use “an” before a singular countable noun that begins with a vowel sound.
cards.example: I saw an elephant in the nature documentary.
options: She packed a umbrella because rain was expected.
She packed an umbrella because rain was expected.
She packed the umbrella because rain was expected.

cards.front: You already said, “I bought a book yesterday.” Complete the next sentence: “___ book is on my desk.”
cards.answer: The book is on my desk.
cards.explanation: Use “the” because the book has already been introduced and is now specific.
cards.example: We rented a car. The car was clean and comfortable.
options: A book is on my desk.
An book is on my desk.
The book is on my desk.

cards.front: Complete this first mention of one of several universities: “Maya studies at ___ university in her city.”
cards.answer: Maya studies at a university in her city.
cards.explanation: Use “a” because “university” begins with a consonant sound, even though it starts with a vowel letter.
cards.example: They joined a European research project.
options: Maya studies at a university in her city.
Maya studies at an university in her city.
Maya studies at the university in her city.

cards.front: Complete the sentence about a duration of sixty minutes: “The repair took ___ hour.”
cards.answer: The repair took an hour.
cards.explanation: Use “an” because the initial “h” in “hour” is silent, so the word begins with a vowel sound.
cards.example: We waited for an honest response.
options: The repair took a hour.
The repair took an hour.

cards.front: Complete the statement about the one sun seen from Earth: “___ sun is bright today.”
cards.answer: The sun is bright today.
cards.explanation: Use “the” for something understood as unique in the shared context.
cards.example: The moon was visible above the clouds.
options: A sun is bright today.
An sun is bright today.
The sun is bright today.

cards.front: Complete the sentence that states Omar’s profession: “Omar is ___ doctor.”
cards.answer: Omar is a doctor.
cards.explanation: Use “a” before a singular job title that begins with a consonant sound.
cards.example: Her sister is a designer.
options: Omar is a doctor.
Omar is an doctor.
Omar is the doctor.

cards.front: Complete this request for one non-specific response: “Please give me ___ honest answer.”
cards.answer: Please give me an honest answer.
cards.explanation: Use “an” because “honest” begins with a vowel sound; its initial “h” is silent.
cards.example: It was an honorable decision.
options: Please give me a honest answer.
Please give me an honest answer.
Please give me the honest answer.

cards.front: You lent Sam a specific set of keys. Complete the request: “Please put ___ keys I lent you on the table.”
cards.answer: Please put the keys I lent you on the table.
cards.explanation: Use “the” because the phrase “I lent you” identifies which keys the speaker means.
cards.example: Could you return the folder that I gave you?
options: Please put a keys I lent you on the table.
Please put the keys I lent you on the table.

cards.front: Complete this first mention when no particular sandwich is meant: “I would like ___ sandwich for lunch.”
cards.answer: I would like a sandwich for lunch.
cards.explanation: Use “a” for one non-specific singular countable noun that begins with a consonant sound.
cards.example: He ordered a bowl of soup.
options: I would like a sandwich for lunch.
I would like an sandwich for lunch.
I would like the sandwich for lunch.

cards.front: You already said, “I made a sandwich.” Complete the next sentence: “___ sandwich is in the fridge.”
cards.answer: The sandwich is in the fridge.
cards.explanation: Use “the” because both sentences refer to the same sandwich.
cards.example: I received a package. The package was from my cousin.
options: A sandwich is in the fridge.
An sandwich is in the fridge.
The sandwich is in the fridge.

cards.front: Complete this first mention of one message: “I sent you ___ email with the details.”
cards.answer: I sent you an email with the details.
cards.explanation: Use “an” before the singular noun “email” because it begins with a vowel sound.
cards.example: She added an image to the document.
options: I sent you a email with the details.
I sent you an email with the details.
I sent you the email with the details.

cards.front: Complete the question asking for the station closest to you: “Where is ___ nearest station?”
cards.answer: Where is the nearest station?
cards.explanation: Use “the” with a superlative such as “nearest” when identifying one item as the most extreme in a group.
cards.example: This is the shortest route to the park.
options: Where is a nearest station?
Where is an nearest station?
Where is the nearest station?

cards.front: Complete this first mention of one helpful document: “The website has ___ useful guide.”
cards.answer: The website has a useful guide.
cards.explanation: Use “a” because “useful” begins with a consonant sound, even though it starts with a vowel letter.
cards.example: We found a user-friendly map online.
options: The website has a useful guide.
The website has an useful guide.
The website has the useful guide.

cards.front: Complete this first mention of one piece of fruit: “Noah packed ___ apple for the trip.”
cards.answer: Noah packed an apple for the trip.
cards.explanation: Use “an” before a singular countable noun that begins with a vowel sound.
cards.example: I added an orange to my lunch bag.
options: Noah packed a apple for the trip.
Noah packed an apple for the trip.
Noah packed the apple for the trip.

cards.front: There is one door in the room. Complete the request about that door: “Please close ___ door before you leave.”
cards.answer: Please close the door before you leave.
cards.explanation: Use “the” because the context identifies one specific door shared by the speaker and listener.
cards.example: Please turn off the light in this room.
options: Please close a door before you leave.
Please close an door before you leave.
Please close the door before you leave.

cards.front: Complete this first mention of one possible suggestion: “Lina had ___ idea for the project.”
cards.answer: Lina had an idea for the project.
cards.explanation: Use “an” before the singular noun “idea” because it begins with a vowel sound.
cards.example: The group discussed an option for reducing costs.
options: Lina had a idea for the project.
Lina had an idea for the project.
Lina had the idea for the project.

cards.front: Complete this first request for one ticket: “I need ___ one-way ticket for tomorrow.”
cards.answer: I need a one-way ticket for tomorrow.
cards.explanation: Use “a” because “one” begins with a consonant sound, even though it starts with a vowel letter.
cards.example: We took a one-hour break after lunch.
options: I need a one-way ticket for tomorrow.
I need an one-way ticket for tomorrow.
I need the one-way ticket for tomorrow.

cards.front: You spoke to one manager yesterday. Complete the sentence about that person: “___ manager will call me today.”
cards.answer: The manager will call me today.
cards.explanation: Use “the” because the earlier conversation identifies the particular manager.
cards.example: I met a technician on Monday. The technician fixed the issue.
options: A manager will call me today.
An manager will call me today.
The manager will call me today.

cards.front: Complete this first mention of one friend from the past: “I met ___ old friend at the station.”
cards.answer: I met an old friend at the station.
cards.explanation: Use “an” before the singular phrase “old friend” because “old” begins with a vowel sound.
cards.example: She received an unexpected message this morning.
options: I met a old friend at the station.
I met an old friend at the station.
I met the old friend at the station.
